## Overview

Heart failure remains a major cardiovascular health challenge, with significant morbidity, mortality, and healthcare burden. Despite advances in evidence-based therapies, gaps remain between guideline recommendations and routine clinical practice.

This ongoing study evaluates adherence to ESC guideline-directed heart failure management among hospitalised patients in tertiary care settings in Bangladesh.

## Study Design

| **Component** | **Description** |
|---|---|
| Design | Multicentre cross-sectional observational study |
| Population | Adults with confirmed heart failure |
| Setting | Tertiary referral hospitals in Bangladesh |
| Sample size | 422 participants |
| Duration | 12 months |

## Research Objectives

- Assess adherence to guideline-recommended heart failure management.
- Evaluate implementation of pharmacological and non-pharmacological therapies.
- Identify factors associated with variation in guideline adherence.

## Methodology

Data are collected using a structured guideline-based semi-structured questionnaire.

## Expected Contribution

This study aims to describe real-world heart failure care practices and identify areas where evidence-based recommendations can be strengthened in resource-limited healthcare settings.

## Research Area

- Cardiology
- Heart Failure
- Clinical Epidemiology
- Healthcare Quality Improvement
- Implementation Science
